acceptance_criteria.text: Given existing Orders in the Order book, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then the response includes counts for placed, shipped, delivered and cancelled Orders across all existing Orders.

Given no existing Orders, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then the response includes placed, shipped, delivered and cancelled counts of 0 and a Non-cancelled total value of 0 cents.

Given existing Orders in the Order book and any Customer filter or Order status filter used for returned Orders, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then the Order book summary is calculated across all existing Orders without applying those filters.

Given there are no Orders for one or more of placed, shipped, delivered or cancelled, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then the response still includes each absent Order status with a count of 0.
Given an Order has Order status placed, shipped, delivered or cancelled, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then that Order contributes 1 to the matching Order status count.
Given an Order has Order status outside placed, shipped, delivered and cancelled, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then that Order does not contribute to any Order status count.

Given existing Orders with Order status placed, shipped or delivered, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then the Non-cancelled total value equals the sum of their full stored values in cents.
Given existing Orders with Order status cancelled, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then cancelled Orders do not contribute to the Non-cancelled total value.

Given an Order has an Order status outside placed, shipped, delivered and cancelled, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then that Order does not contribute to the Non-cancelled total value.

Given an Order with Order status placed, shipped or delivered has a missing or null stored value, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then that Order contributes 0 cents to the Non-cancelled total value.

Given an Order with Order status placed, shipped or delivered has a negative stored value, when a Support lead requests the Order book summary, then that Order contributes the negative value exactly as stored to the Non-cancelled total value.

stories.description: Add store-level summary calculation, response models, route handling, deterministic tests, and regenerated OpenAPI contract for GET /orders/summary. The summary is global across all existing Orders and returns status counts plus Non-cancelled total value without adding storage, authentication, pagination, or logging customer data.

tests.name: GET /orders/summary returns global status counts and non-cancelled total for existing orders
GET /orders/summary returns zero counts and zero total when order book is empty
GET /orders/summary is not affected by order retrieval customer or status filters
GET /orders/summary includes absent supported statuses with zero counts
GET /orders/summary excludes unsupported statuses from counts and total
GET /orders/summary treats missing or null non-cancelled stored values as zero
GET /orders/summary includes negative non-cancelled stored values exactly
OpenAPI documents GET /orders/summary response schema with all status counts and non-cancelled total

parameters.expected: Path GET /orders/summary exists; successful response schema requires counts for placed, shipped, delivered, cancelled and non_cancelled_total_value_cents as integer cents

stories.title: Add global Order book summary endpoint

acceptance_criteria.text: Given Orders with stored Customer names, when a Support lead requests Orders with a non-blank Customer filter, then the response includes only Orders whose stored Customer name exactly matches the trimmed Customer filter value with the same letter casing.
Given an Order with Customer name `Alice`, when a Support lead requests Orders with Customer filter value ` Alice `, then the Order is included in the response.
Given an Order with Customer name `Alice`, when a Support lead requests Orders with Customer filter value `alice`, then the Order is not included in the response.
Given a non-blank Customer filter and no matching Orders, when a Support lead requests Orders, then the system returns a successful response with no Orders.
Given Orders with missing or null Customer names, when a Support lead requests Orders with a non-blank Customer filter, then those Orders are not included in the response.

Given Orders with missing or null Customer names that are returned when no Customer filter is applied, when a Support lead requests Orders without a Customer filter, then those Orders remain in the response.
Given a blank or whitespace-only Customer filter value, when a Support lead requests Orders, then no Customer filter is applied.

Given both a non-blank Customer filter and an Order status filter are provided, when a Support lead requests Orders, then the response includes only Orders matching both the trimmed exact Customer name and the requested Order status.
Given only an Order status filter is provided, when a Support lead requests Orders, then only the Order status filter is applied.
Given no Customer filter is provided, when a Support lead requests Orders, then no Customer filter is applied.

stories.description: Extend the existing GET /orders implementation with an optional customer query parameter, update store filtering to trim and exact-match Customer name while preserving existing status-filter behavior, add deterministic tests, and regenerate OpenAPI contract version 1.1.0 with the additive parameter.

tests.name: GET /orders with non-blank customer returns only exact case-sensitive customer matches after trimming
GET /orders trims leading and trailing spaces from customer filter
GET /orders with non-blank customer and no matches succeeds with empty orders
GET /orders excludes missing or null customer names when non-blank customer filter is provided
GET /orders without customer filter returns orders with missing or null customer names
GET /orders treats blank or whitespace-only customer filter as no customer filter
GET /orders with customer and status filters returns only orders matching both
GET /orders with only status filter applies only status filter
OpenAPI documents optional customer query parameter on GET /orders without removing status filter

parameters.expected: GET /orders has optional customer query parameter; existing optional status query parameter remains documented; successful response schema for returned orders remains compatible
